rubrics.justification: It correctly recognizes a very poor-quality early blastocyst with poorly defined ICM/TE, but it misstates Gardner expansion 1 as blastocoel less than half the embryo despite the provided definition saying at least half, and it overcalls specific degeneration/apoptosis features not reliably discernible from the image alone.

The response integrates age, AMH, oocyte maturity, male-factor context, and lifestyle reasonably well, though some links are speculative (PCOS, trigger issue, sperm DNA fragmentation) without supporting data.

The overall logic is structured, but there are notable issues: it labels the embryo definitively non-viable and predicts essentially zero implantation from morphology alone, and some conclusions extend beyond the available evidence.

Much of the discussion is broadly consistent with IVF practice, but stating the embryo is categorically unsuitable/non-viable and recommending cancellation solely on this basis is stronger than standard morphology-based guidance; some protocol and PGT-A recommendations are also somewhat overgeneralized.

It provides clear next-step suggestions for counseling, protocol review, sperm workup, and future cycle planning, though the immediate recommendation to cancel transfer is overly absolute and not sufficiently nuanced.
